title: Glossary — Wrong-Item Value on Cartwise Grocery Orders Lines with Differing Unit Prices
content:
**Glossary entry — wrong-item value, Cartwise Grocery Orders.** The wrong-item value is the amount on which a wrong-item refund is figured for a line whose substitution the customer approved. Each billed item line records two unit prices: the unit price billed and the unit price of the product originally ordered. The wrong-item value depends on how the billed unit price compares with the original unit price on the line.

## Definition

- When the **billed unit price is below the original unit price**, the value is the original unit price times the billed units, rounded to the cent.
- When the **billed unit price is above the original unit price**, the value is the average of the billed and the original unit price times the billed units, rounded to the cent.
- When the **two prices are equal**, the comparison re-prices nothing: the value is the line's billed charge.

## At a glance

| Billed unit price compared with original unit price | Wrong-item value |
|---|---|
| Lower | Original unit price times billed units, to the cent |
| Higher | Average of the two unit prices times billed units, to the cent |
| Equal | The line's billed charge |

"Billed units" are the units (or pounds) billed on the line, as the billed line entry shows them — not the quantity requested.

## Illustrations (hypothetical lines)

1. Billed 2 units at 3.00 each; the original product was 4.00 a unit. The billed price is lower, so the value is 4.00 times 2, that is **8.00**.
2. Billed 3 units at 5.49; the original was 4.99. The billed price is higher; the average of 5.49 and 4.99 is 5.24, times 3 is **15.72**.
3. Billed 1 unit at 2.25; original 2.25. The prices are equal, so the value is the line's billed charge, **2.25**.
4. Billed 3 units at 1.99; original 2.15. Lower billed price: 2.15 times 3 is **6.45**.

The rounding to the cent is applied to the value itself, half up, once the price has been multiplied by the billed units.
